gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured runtime for any small UPS or a measured NAS power draw. Legit Reviews kept a roughly 30 W load running for 75 minutes on the APC BE600M1, and Notebookcheck measured a two-bay NAS with two WD Red drives at 14.84–20.14 W idle and 35.9 W flat out, so a 600 VA unit covers a 2–5 minute shutdown timer many times over.
standout_why: I read the cited holdbackup.com guide, racksandwatts.com and techfromalex.com. HoldBackup says it tested nothing and uses only CyberPower's 66 min at 100 W rating for the CP1500PFCLCD. Racks and Watts declines to give any runtime and lists only datasheet waveforms. Tech from Alex gives a 3-minute full-load CP850PFCLCD figure without naming a source. The cited Synology compatibility and KB pages have no measurements. None of these pages has a named runtime test of a small UPS, a measured transfer time, or a measured NAS wall draw.
decides: The measurements back the smallest AC pick. A two-bay NAS measures about 5.6 W (igor'sLAB, standby, NVMe only) to 35.9 W (Notebookcheck, maximum). The BE600M1 ran 75 minutes on about 30 W (Legit Reviews), so buying an 850 VA unit for runtime is unnecessary. Pick the 850 VA class only if you want pure sine output. Custom PC Review measured the CP1500PFCLCD's switchover at about 8–11 ms against a 4 ms rating, so a page that leans on the CyberPower PFC line's 4 ms figure should be careful. For the UGREEN US3000, no reviewer has timed a runtime. The 'about 10 minutes' figure is UGREEN's, NASCompares repeats it, and NASCompares measured only that the outage was logged in under 2 seconds.

findings.label: Runtime on battery, reviewer test
findings.source_title: APC UPS 600VA BE600M1 Battery Backup & Surge Protector Review (Legit Reviews, Nathan Kirsch, 2018-12-10)
findings.note: The load was a router, a camera system and a cable modem. The 30 W is the sum of the devices' rated draws (18 + 5 + 6 W), not a meter reading. In the same article APC rates 67 min at 40 W and 23 min at 100 W.

findings.product: general (2-bay NAS: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 GT)
findings.label: NAS wall draw, idle and maximum
findings.value: 14.84–20.14 W idle; 31.12 W all CPU cores loaded; 35.9 W CPU and drives at full load
findings.source_title: Small, fast and surprisingly quiet: Ugreen NASync DXP2800 GT review (Notebookcheck, Daniel Schmidt, 2026-10-13)
findings.note: Two WD Red HDDs installed and spinning during idle. Arithmetic: 35.9 W is about 11% of the BE600M1's 330 W rating.

findings.label: NAS wall draw
findings.value: 0.6 W off with WoL; 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during data transfer
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test, page 8 (igor'sLAB, Tim Kutzner, 2024-05-08)
findings.note: Measured at the wall socket with one NVMe SSD and no HDDs, so hard drives add to these figures. The DXP2800 is one of the NASes the US2000 is listed for.

findings.label: NAS energy use over 24 h
findings.value: about 275 Wh per 24 h (about 11.5 W average)
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ review (Dong Knows Tech, Dong Ngo, 2025-08-04)
findings.note: Tested with two hard drives. The method is not described. Average is 275 Wh ÷ 24 h ≈ 11.5 W.

findings.label: Outage detection, reviewer test
findings.value: outage logged by the NAS in under 2 s
findings.source_title: UGREEN US3000 NAS UPS Review (NASCompares, Rob Andrews, 2025-09-26)
findings.note: From the review's power-pull test. The 5-minute timed shutdown was a setting, not a measurement. The review's 'up to around ten minutes' runtime has no stated NAS, drives or load.

findings.product: general (CyberPower CP1500PFCLCD, larger sibling of the CP850PFCLCD)
findings.label: Measured transfer time, runtime and waveform
findings.value: about 8–11 ms transfer (rated 4 ms); 24 min at 200 W; pure sine output on battery
findings.source_title: CyberPower CP1500 AVR LCD and CP1500 PFC LCD review (Custom PC Review, Sam Chen, 2017-04-30)
findings.note: Load built from chained 50 W fluorescent bulbs, waveform checked on an oscilloscope. This is the 1500 VA model, not the CP850PFCLCD. Use it only as a family data point.
